messages:
elle (DevEx): quick q — running integration test against local dockerized server, getting 401 on auth. i set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env but when i print the header it looks like there might be a hidden newline. anyone seen trailing/newline chars leak into a basic auth header?

repro i used locally:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"$(cat ~/.redwood/key.txt)\"
curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $(echo -n ":$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | base64)\" http://localhost:8000/v1/health
```

it works when i run that in my shell. when the same logic runs from a systemd unit it returns 401. printing the header from the server shows an extra char at the end. :thinking_face:

aj: can you `cat -v` the key file to check for hidden chars? often you get `^M` or trailing newline. `echo -n` helps in shell but subshells + systemd env parsing can be different. try `tr -d '\r\n'` or `xargs` to strip.

kai: also check how systemd loads the variable. `EnvironmentFile` will include the newline char if the file has one. if you're doing `EnvironmentFile=/etc/redwood/keyfile` and that file contains `REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` ending with a newline, systemd will export it literally. prefer storing raw secret and trimming on ExecStart.

elle (DevEx): ran `cat -v ~/.redwood/key.txt` — shows `mysecretkey$` (so newline present). when i changed the unit to run `ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c 'KEY=$(tr -d "\\r\\n" < /etc/redwood/key.txt); export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$KEY"'` the service started returning 200. odd that interactive shell didn't need trimming.

infra-bot: note: systemd behavior: EnvironmentFile accepts `KEY=val` pairs; trailing newline is part of file formatting and may be exported. best practice: keep secrets without trailing newlines or explicitly trim in unit.

aj: small, robust patterns i use:
```bash
# safe read and curl usage in scripts
KEY=$(tr -d '\\r\\n' < /path/to/key.txt)
AUTH=$(printf ':%s' "$KEY" | base64 -w 0) # -w 0 or base64 -A to avoid wrap
curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $AUTH\" http://localhost:8000/v1/health
```
# or in systemd ExecStart directly
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'KEY=$(tr -d "\\r\\n" < /etc/redwood/key.txt); exec /usr/bin/myapp'
```

kai: node sdk note: we've seen folks pass env vars with trailing whitespace into clients and get 401s. defensively `.trim()` env values at client init if you expect human-managed secret files. also watch BOMs (UTF-8 BOM) and CRLF from windows editors. `sed -e 's/\r$//'` is handy.

elle (DevEx): good call. i'll add a tiny troubleshooting blurb to the devex auth docs: mention systemd envfile gotcha, suggested `tr -d` snippet, and node sdk `.trim()` tip. want me to PR into quickstart and the sdk readme?

aj: +1 from me, happy to review.

kai: +1, please include example for base64 `-w 0` and `openssl base64 -A` variants so people don't get wrapped lines.

elle (DevEx): awesome — i'll open PR after standup. thanks all :+1:
